'''Jacques Prost''', born in 1946 in [[Bourg-en-Bresse]], is a French physicist, former General director of [[École supérieure de physique et de chimie industrielles de la ville de Paris]], member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/membres/p/prost_jacques_bio.htm |title=French Academy of Sciences |access-date=2009-03-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081206072854/http://www.academie-sciences.fr/membres/P/Prost_Jacques_bio.htm |archive-date=2008-12-06 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Alumni of the [[École Normale Supérieure de Lyon|École normale supérieure de Saint-Cloud (sciences)]] (1965), Jacques Prost studied at [[Harvard University]] and founded and head (1987–1995) the "Theoretical Physico-Chemistry" Group<ref>[http://www.pct.espci.fr/en/ Theoretical Physico-Chemistry Group at the ESPCI] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081125192010/http://www.pct.espci.fr/en/ |date=2008-11-25 }}</ref> of the ESPCI ParisTech under the direction of [[Pierre-Gilles de Gennes]]. His group studied [[liquid crystal]]<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=0Nw-dzWz5agC&q=jacques+prost+liquid+crystal The Physics of liquid crystal, PG de Gennes, J. Prost, Oxford University Press]</ref> and [[soft matter]] properties. In 1996, he founded the group "Physical Chemistry Curie" lab<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.curie.fr/recherche/themes/detail_equipe.cfm/lang/_gb/id_equipe/66.htm |title=Prost group at Curie Institute |access-date=2009-03-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090310190805/http://www.curie.fr/recherche/themes/detail_equipe.cfm/lang/_gb/id_equipe/66.htm |archive-date=2009-03-10 |url-status=dead }}</ref> at the [[Curie Institute (Paris)]]. His group studies physical approaches to biological problems and describes cell motion, [[molecular motors]], the properties of [[biological membrane]]s and [[protein]] adhesion.

Jacques Prost was the scientific advisor to [[Elf Aquitaine]] from 1990 to 1999. He is a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] since 2007. Jacques Prost has been the General director of [[ESPCI|ESPCI ParisTech]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.espci.fr/presentation/index_en.htm |title=ESPCI ParisTech |access-date=2009-03-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090330021500/http://www.espci.fr/presentation/index_en.htm |archive-date=2009-03-30 |url-status=dead }}</ref> since 2003.

He is the recipient of the 2024 [[Lars Onsager Prize]] in theoretical statistical physics by the [[American Physical Society]], for<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-25 |title=Congratulations to the 2024 Lars Onsager Prize recipient! |url=https://engage.aps.org/gsnp/blogs/emma-rosa-zajdela/2023/10/25/congratulations-to-the-2024-onsager-prize-recipie |access-date=2023-11-23 |website=engage.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>

{{Quote2|influential contributions to the statistical physics of nonequilibrium phenomena and applications to soft matter and biological systems.}}
